turns.content: Find the intersection points of x=x and y=x^2 that bound a finite region.
On the enclosed interval, determine which curve is above the other and identify the outer and inner radii when the region is rotated about the x-axis.
Explain why a cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a washer rather than a solid disk, using the two boundary curves in your explanation.
Confirm that slices perpendicular to the x-axis match the stated rotation axis, and explain why the washer method is more direct than cylindrical shells for this setup.
Write the washer slice dV=pi(R^2-r^2)dx, identify R and r for this region, and explain their ordering from the geometry.
Substitute the two radii into the washer formula, simplify the cross-sectional area, and set up the definite integral for the volume without evaluating it.
Find an antiderivative of the integrand and evaluate it at the intersection bounds to obtain the exact volume.
Check that the result is positive and has the correct cubic units, and compare its size with a simple enclosing cylinder as a plausibility check.
Report the exact volume and a decimal approximation, together with the integral from which they follow.
